A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of all equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting and genomic-classification experiments, acceleration measurements, and ablations in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including transformer, Chronos, Hyena, Mamba, and supplementary PatchTST evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical global, local, causal, and dynamic token-merging procedures, including decoder unmerging. The accompanying method details in Appendices B and C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and genomic classification on Dummy Mouse Enhancers Ensembl. Appendix scenarios, including the trend and periodicity examples, are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments, including no-merging and global-merging controls in Table 3, Gaussian filtering in Figures 6 and 17, and local pruning in Figure 16.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same splits, 7,000-series Chronos sample, input and prediction lengths, model sizes, training budgets, tuning and selection procedures, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Section 6 and the appendices retain the same analyses of smoothing, spectral properties, token similarity, pruning, tokenization, positional embeddings, and input length. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both specify seed 2024 in Table 6 and two measurement runs per batch after two warm-ups in Appendix C, with inference-time standard deviation generally below 2%. Uncertainty reporting and repeat counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are identical, including the appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains the 54.76× Weather acceleration with a 3% MSE increase, and Table 3 retains identical Hyena and Mamba results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and complexity expressions in Section 3 and the complexity and speed-up derivations in Appendix B.1 are identical. No assumptions or mathematical reasoning are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about time-series token merging, causal local merging, spectral predictors, and efficiency and accuracy benefits. Their scientific scope and claimed novelty are unchanged.

C2.justification: The low-pass-filter interpretation, spectral and token-similarity explanations, and scientific limitations are unchanged. The new Volkswagen disclaimer concerns institutional endorsement and adds no scientific qualification or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Tables 6–7 preserve identical hyperparameters, implementation instructions, hardware, timing procedures, and GPU-hour estimates. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: No cited work is added or removed, and Section 2 and Appendix A retain the same research positioning. Bibliography entries merely reflow across columns and pages.

P1.justification: v4 adds Munich Center for Machine Learning affiliations for Marcel Kollovieh and Stephan Günnemann, adds a Volkswagen disclaimer on page 9, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The affiliation addition changes first-page typesetting, and the disclaimer shifts the references on pages 9–10. All figures and tables retain their content, design, captions, and placement; appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 adds affiliation and institutional-disclaimer information with limited layout changes. Methods, theoretical reasoning, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and scientific limitations—including all appendices—are unchanged. These administrative edits do not materially improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
